note: Practice questions (Claude-drafted, original wording) for A1 and A2, 300 per level, written to the CEFR scope of each level (grammar and vocabulary in line with the English Grammar Profile / English Vocabulary Profile level descriptions) with everyday British contexts. Imported as drafts for teacher review.

passages.A1P_MAYA: Maya is nine. She lives in Bristol with her mum and her grandfather. Every morning her grandfather takes her to school. Maya's favourite lesson is art. She doesn't like maths. After school she plays with her dog, Biscuit, in the park. On Sundays she visits her dad in Bath.
passages.A1P_CAFE: Rosie's Café. Breakfast 8 – 11 am. Lunch 12 – 3 pm. Tea and coffee £2. Sandwiches £4.50. Soup of the day £3.50. Closed on Mondays. Free Wi-Fi.
passages.A1P_JOE: Hi, I'm Joe. I'm a bus driver in Manchester. I start work at six in the morning, so I get up very early. I finish at two o'clock. In the afternoon I sleep for an hour and then I cook dinner. My wife is a teacher. We have two sons, Leo and Max.
passages.A1P_WEEKEND: Last weekend was great. On Saturday I went to the market with my sister. We bought fruit and a new bag for her. In the evening we watched a film at home. On Sunday it rained, so we stayed in and played board games. I was very tired on Monday!
passages.A1P_SIGN: SWIMMING POOL. Open every day 7 am – 9 pm. Children under 8 must be with an adult. No food or drinks in the pool area. Please have a shower before you swim.
passages.A1P_FLAT: I live in a flat on the third floor. It has two bedrooms, a kitchen, a small bathroom and a living room. There is no garden, but there is a balcony with lots of plants. The flat is near the station, so I walk to the train every day.
passages.A1P_TEXT: Hi Tom! I'm at the supermarket. Do we need anything? I've got milk, eggs and tomatoes. Do we have rice? Text me before 5 pm. See you at home. Dad
passages.A1P_PEN: My pen friend's name is Aiko. She is 15 and she lives in Osaka, in Japan. She has one brother. She likes music and she plays the piano. Her favourite food is sushi. She wants to visit London next summer.
passages.A1P_CLASS: Our English class is on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6 to 8 pm. The teacher is Mr Green. There are twelve students in the class. They come from six countries. After the class some students go to the café for a cup of tea.
passages.A1P_LOST: LOST! Small black cat. Her name is Luna. She has a white nose and a red collar. She was last seen on Hill Road on Friday evening. Please call Ben on 07700 900456.
passages.A1P_MARKET: The Saturday market is in the town square. It opens at 8 am and closes at 2 pm. You can buy fresh fruit, vegetables, cheese and flowers. There is also a stall with hot food. Many people go there for breakfast.
passages.A1P_TRIP: Dear Grandma, We are in Cornwall! Our hotel is next to the beach. The weather is warm and sunny. Every day we swim in the sea and eat ice cream. Yesterday Dad took us on a boat. Tomorrow we are going to a castle. Love, Emma
passages.A1P_BUS: Bus 22 to the City Centre. Monday to Saturday: every 15 minutes from 6 am to 7 pm, then every 30 minutes until 11 pm. Sunday: every hour from 9 am to 6 pm. Single ticket £2. Day ticket £5.
passages.A1P_NEW: Hello, I'm Daniel. I'm new at this school. I'm from Poland but I live in Leeds now. I speak Polish and a little English. I like football and computer games. I'm in class 7B. Can somebody help me find the library?
passages.A1P_DIALOGUE: Assistant: Good morning. Can I help you? — Customer: Yes, please. I'd like a ticket to Oxford. — Assistant: Single or return? — Customer: Return, please. — Assistant: That's £18. — Customer: Can I pay by card? — Assistant: Of course. The train leaves from platform 4 at 10:15.
passages.A1P_DAYOFF: Nadia works in a hotel from Monday to Friday. Saturday is her day off. On Saturday morning she sleeps late and has a big breakfast. Then she phones her mother in Egypt. In the afternoon she goes shopping or meets her friends. She goes to bed early because on Sunday she has a cooking class.
passages.A1P_NOTICE: Library News. The library is closed on Friday 12th May for cleaning. From Monday 15th May there are new opening times: Monday to Friday 9 am – 7 pm, Saturday 10 am – 4 pm. You can now borrow ten books at a time.
passages.A2P_MOVE: Six months ago Carlos moved from Madrid to Edinburgh to study engineering. At first he found it difficult: the weather was cold and wet, and he didn't understand the Scottish accent. He also missed his family and Spanish food. But now he has made friends from many countries, and he has joined a hiking club. Last month he climbed Arthur's Seat, a hill in the middle of the city, and saw the whole of Edinburgh. He says his English has improved a lot because he only speaks English at university.
passages.A2P_ADVERT: WANTED: Part-time waiter or waitress for a busy Italian restaurant in York. Evenings and weekends, about 20 hours a week. No experience needed — we will train you. You must be friendly, polite and over 18. Pay: £11 an hour plus tips. Free meal every shift. Send your CV to jobs@example.com before 30th June.
passages.A2P_EMAIL: Hi Sam, Thanks for inviting me to your party on Saturday. I'd love to come, but I'm afraid I'll be a bit late. I have to work until 7, and then I need to go home and change. I'll probably arrive at about 8.30. Is that OK? Shall I bring something? I could make my chocolate cake — everyone liked it last time! See you soon, Lily
passages.A2P_GYM: FitLife Gym — New Year Offer! Join before 31st January and pay only £20 a month (normal price £30). Open 6 am – 10 pm every day. Free fitness classes: yoga on Mondays, dance on Wednesdays, boxing on Fridays. Students get a further 10% off. Bring a photo and your bank details to join.
passages.A2P_HISTORY: Stonehenge is a famous circle of large stones in the south of England. People started building it about 5,000 years ago. Some of the stones came from Wales, more than 200 kilometres away. Nobody knows exactly how people moved them or why they built it. Some experts think it was a kind of calendar, because on the longest day of the year the sun rises in line with the stones. Today more than a million people visit it every year.
passages.A2P_PROBLEM: Dear Sir or Madam, Last week I bought a coffee machine from your online shop. When it arrived, I noticed that the box was damaged. I tried to use the machine, but it didn't work. I would like to return it and get my money back. Could you tell me how to send it back? My order number is 45721. Yours faithfully, P. Ahmed
passages.A2P_DIARY: Monday: I started my new job today. My manager, Jane, showed me the office and introduced me to everyone. I had lunch with two colleagues, Raj and Ellie. The work was more difficult than I expected, but everyone was helpful. Tuesday: I arrived late because my train was delayed. I felt terrible, but Jane said it wasn't a problem. In the afternoon I wrote my first report.
passages.A2P_ISLAND: The Isle of Skye is an island off the west coast of Scotland. It is famous for its mountains, waterfalls and castles. You can get there by car over a bridge, so you don't need to take a boat. The weather changes quickly, so visitors should bring warm clothes and waterproofs, even in summer. In August the island is very busy, so it is best to book accommodation early.
passages.A2P_RECIPE: Easy pancakes (makes 8). You need: 100 g flour, 2 eggs, 300 ml milk, a little oil. First, put the flour in a bowl and add the eggs. Then slowly add the milk and mix well. Heat a little oil in a frying pan. Pour in some of the mixture and cook for one minute on each side. Serve with lemon and sugar.
passages.A2P_VOLUNTEER: Every Saturday morning, Grace volunteers at an animal shelter near Cardiff. She walks the dogs, cleans the cages and helps visitors who want to adopt a pet. She started two years ago because she couldn't have a dog in her flat. 'It's the best part of my week,' she says. 'The animals are so happy to see me.' Last year Grace helped find homes for more than thirty dogs.
passages.A2P_TRAINS: Dear passengers, because of engineering work, there will be no trains between Bath and Bristol this Sunday. A bus service will replace the trains. Buses will leave from outside the main entrance every 20 minutes. Journeys will take about 30 minutes longer than usual. Tickets for the train are valid on the bus. We are sorry for any inconvenience.
passages.A2P_TWINS: Ruth and Rachel are twins, but they are very different. Ruth is outgoing and loves parties, while Rachel is quiet and prefers reading at home. Ruth studied business and now works in a bank in London. Rachel became a vet and lives in a small village in Devon. They talk on the phone every evening and spend every Christmas together.
passages.A2P_PARK: Welcome to Greenfield Park. Please keep dogs on a lead near the children's playground. Cycling is allowed only on the marked paths. Barbecues are not permitted. The café is open from 9 am to 5 pm in summer and from 10 am to 3 pm in winter. Free guided walks start at the main gate every Sunday at 11 am.
passages.A2P_INVENTION: The first successful telephone call was made by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876. Bell was born in Edinburgh in 1847 and later moved to Canada and then to the United States. His mother and his wife were both deaf, and much of his work was about helping deaf people communicate. Today, more than five billion people around the world use a mobile phone.
passages.A2P_CLUB: The Hilltop Book Club meets on the first Thursday of every month at 7 pm in the community centre. Each month we read one novel and then discuss it together over tea and biscuits. New members are always welcome. You don't need to buy the books — the local library keeps copies for us. This month's book is 'The Secret Garden'.
passages.A2P_ADVICE: Q: I want to save money but I always spend everything by the end of the month. What can I do? — A: First, write down everything you spend for a month. You'll be surprised how much goes on coffee and snacks! Then decide on a small amount to save each week, even £5, and put it in a separate account as soon as you are paid. Finally, try cooking at home more often instead of buying lunch.
passages.A2P_SPORTS: Our school sports day was last Friday. The weather was perfect — sunny but not too hot. There were running races, the long jump and a tug of war between the teachers and the students. The students won the tug of war for the first time in ten years! My class came second overall, just behind class 9C. After the events, parents sold cakes to raise money for new football shirts.
